simple.meaning: פּוּךְ (pûwk) is a Hebrew word meaning “dye (specifically, stibium for the eyes).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: פּוּךְ (H6320) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 2 Kings 9:30, with occurrences in 2 Kings, 1 Chronicles, Isaiah, Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פּוּךְ (H6320) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in פּוּךְ (H6320) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: פּוּךְ (pûwk) / H6320 is traced through 2 Kings 9:30, 1 Chronicles 29:2, Isaiah 54:11, Jeremiah 4:30 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H6320. puk מּוּךְ noun [masculine] antimony, stibium (Late Hebrew = Biblical Hebrew; compare possibly Arabic open, separate ; Syriac pulverize ; but מּוּךְ perhaps foreign word); — black mineral powder, for increasing brilliance of eyes by darkening edges of lids; עֵינֶוהָ בֵּמּ ׳וַתָּשֶׂם 2Kin 9:30 , וגו ׳תִּקְרְעִי Jer 4:30 ; (on practice in Arabic see We GGN, 1893, 443 ; in Egypt, Lane Mod.Egypt.ed. 5, i. 45 f. ); figurative Isa 54:11 of dark cement setting off precious stones (but We DLZ, Aug. 2, 1890 Che Hpt and others read נֹפֶךְ q. v.); פ ׳אַבְנֵי 1Chr 29:2 are perhaps stones of brilliant hue of antimony. — compare proper name הַמּוּךְ קֶרֶן , and כָּחַל .
